description: guard hooks. Logic lives in `scripts/guard_hook.py`; see `dev/design.md` for the design.

hooks.description: Name the file this turn's answer is written to, so the audit has something editable to correct. Silent when every agent is off, when the session is muted, and on guard's own control commands. guard keeps no copy of the prompt.
Mute or unmute guard's automatic audit for this session (arg: on|off, empty flips).
On demand, dispatch the claims auditor for the last completed turn.
On demand, dispatch the deferrals auditor for the last completed turn.
On demand, dispatch the clarity auditor for the last completed turn.
On demand, dispatch the Korean corrector for the last completed turn.

Deny a write from one of guard's report-only agents (claims-auditor, deferrals-auditor, clarity-auditor, agents-md-auditor, ext-docs-auditor) when the target is outside an agent-memory directory. Declaring `memory:` silently grants those agents Write and Edit, and the host does not scope the grant, so "reports; edits nothing" is enforced here rather than promised in each definition.

When ext-docs-fetcher is on, deny WebFetch/WebSearch from the main conversation and name that agent in the reason. This project saves copies of the documentation it cites, and a standing instruction to delegate the fetch is skippable without a trace; a denied tool call is not. Fails open inside any subagent — a subagent cannot dispatch another agent, so denying its fetch would leave it no way forward.

Record a source file, an agent instruction file, or a saved reference written this turn (for a comment-corrector, agents-md-auditor or ext-docs-auditor recommendation) — a subagent's writes included — and require a file saved inside the refs dir to be listed in the refs index (AGENTS.md).

Mark the finished turn as the on-demand audit target, and — when any agent switch is on — ask the main agent to invoke the `guard:audit` skill for that turn. One line: the dispatch itself is built by the `dispatch` CLI verb inside that skill's forked context, so the roster and the paths are not paid for in the context the user is talking to.

Sweep guard state and turn records past the retention window, export GUARD_REFS_DIR, state the refs rule as session context, and — when ext-docs-fetcher is on — send the session's documentation lookups to that agent instead of its own WebFetch.
